# Micah 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** How miserable I am! I feel like a fruit picker after the harvest — there's nothing left to eat. Not a single grape or early fig to satisfy my hunger.

**2** The faithful have disappeared from the land. There's not an honest person left. Everyone is out for blood, and they all set traps for each other.

**3** Both hands are busy doing evil — and they're good at it! Officials demand bribes. Judges sell their verdicts. The powerful dictate what they want, and they all conspire together.

**4** The best of them is like a brier bush; the most honest is worse than a thorn hedge. But your day of reckoning is here — the day your watchmen warned about. Now is the time of your confusion.

**5** Don't trust your neighbor. Don't confide in your friend. Even be careful what you say to your wife.

**6** For sons treat fathers with contempt. Daughters rebel against mothers. Daughters-in-law turn on mothers-in-law. Your worst enemies are the members of your own family!

**7** But as for me — I will look to the LORD for help. I will wait confidently for God to save me, and my God will hear me.

**8** Don't gloat over me, my enemies! Though I have fallen, I will get back up. Though I sit in the darkness, the LORD will be my light.

**9** I will be patient as the LORD punishes me, because I have sinned against Him. But after that, He will take up my case and see that justice is done for me. He will bring me into the light, and I will see His righteousness.

**10** Then my enemies will see this and be covered with shame — the same enemies who taunted me, 'Where is the LORD your God?' I will see their downfall with my own eyes. They'll be trampled like mud in the streets.

**11** The day to rebuild your walls is coming! On that day your boundaries will be extended far and wide.

**12** People will come to you from everywhere — from Assyria, from Egypt, from all across the earth.

**13** But first the rest of the earth will become desolate because of the evil its inhabitants have done.

**14** LORD, protect Your people with Your shepherd's staff — the flock of Your special possession. Though they live alone in a thicket in the middle of a fertile land, let them graze in the rich pastures of Bashan and Gilead like they did in days gone by.

**15** "Yes, I will do mighty miracles for you, like those I did when I rescued you from Egypt."

**16** All the nations of the world will see what God has done and be put to shame despite all their power. They will stand speechless, covering their mouths in stunned silence.

**17** They will grovel in the dust like snakes crawling on the ground. They will come trembling from their fortresses. They will turn in fear to the LORD our God and be terrified of You.

**18** Where is there another God like You, who pardons the guilt of the remnant of His people? You don't stay angry forever, because You love to show mercy.

**19** Once again You will have compassion on us. You will trample our sins under Your feet and throw them into the depths of the ocean!

**20** You will show us Your faithfulness and unfailing love as You promised to our ancestors Abraham and Jacob long ago.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **7:7-8**: 'Though I fall, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD is my light.' This is biblical hope distilled — not denial of suffering but confidence through it. Two of the most resilient verses in the Bible.

- **7:18**: The last question of the book is the best one: 'Who is a God like You?' — a God who pardons, who doesn't stay angry, who delights in mercy. That's the final word. Not judgment — mercy.

- **7:19**: Sins thrown into the deepest part of the ocean. Gone. Unretrievable. God doesn't just forgive — He disposes of the evidence permanently. The Jewish tashlich ceremony at Rosh Hashanah is built on this very image.

— PNEUMA
